frontmatter.title: A Girl by the Seaside
frontmatter.summary: A short story and poem about a child's simple joy in collecting shells on Lake Michigan, reminding us that true treasures point us to eternity with God.
frontmatter.author: Hope Hanson

articles.content:
# A Girl by the Seaside

She ran along the shore, a squeal of delight escaping her lips at every shell she came upon. One chubby fist held the edge of her blue skirt in a bundle, creating a little pouch to hold her treasures. Silver shells, white shells, blue shells, perfect shells, soft shells, big shells, small shells. Broken shells too. All slipped into the makeshift bag.

She sat upon the sun warmed beach, wiggling her toes in the soft sand. One by one, she laid the shells out on the ground as the icy cold waves leapt against the shore of Lake Michigan a little ways in front of her. Her rosy cheeks spread in a wide, contented smile. A gusty wind blew across her face, whipping stray blond hairs wildly like the brown and green grasses around her.

***

She wishes for a shell to find\
Along the golden sand,\
A treasure with worth beyond all measure\
To hold within her hand.

A child's treasure in a shell\
Is greater than a miser's gold,\
For God made shells and trees and grass\
Real treasures to behold.

But even these cannot compare\
To God's ultimate treasure.\
Eternity with Him above\
And joy beyond all measure!

***

*By Hope Hanson*

frontmatter.title: A Wild Tail: How a Cartoon Created Japan''s Raccoon Problem
frontmatter.summary: The unexpected true story of how a 1977 Japanese cartoon based on a Wisconsin memoir accidentally introduced an invasive raccoon population to Japan.
frontmatter.author: Andrew Rocke

articles.content:
# A Wild Tail

So, I'm the kind of person that when I watch a movie or hear about something that interests me, I'll often do a little online research to learn more about the topic. Recently, my wife and I watched the movie *Rascal* together. It is based on the book with a similar name. We had briefly talked about it for a few minutes afterwards when I took up my computer to do a little investigation.

## The Original Story

*Rascal: A Memoir of a Better Era* was written by Sterling North in 1963. It is based on his childhood experience of raising a baby raccoon in Wisconsin during World War I. The book won several awards, and the movie was made in 1969. As I perused the Wikipedia article, I noticed that a Japanese cartoon was based on the book and "was responsible for the accidental introduction of the raccoon into Japan."¹ That piqued my interest.

## An Unintended Consequence

A short internet search found a 2024 Fox News article entitled: "Japan grappling with invasive raccoon population." Sure enough, the 1977 cartoon called *Rascal the Raccoon* (in English) was responsible for the importation of raccoons as pets and, thus, the introduction of an invasive species in Japan (hey, they are kind of cute – as long as you don't think about all the damage they do and problems they cause).

As could be imagined, the Japanese owners discovered that raccoons don't make good pets. When quoting Jaime Arslan, a raccoon owner, the article says:

> Raccoons... "can be very destructive in a home" and need to be constantly entertained. Additionally, raccoons "can and will bite," either as aggression or as a form of play. Their care, too, is extremely expensive, as most veterinarians will not see a raccoon."²

## History Repeats Itself

So, history repeated itself and the Japanese did what Sterling had to do with his raccoon: they let them go in the wild.

***

## References

¹ Wikipedia contributors, "Rascal (book)," *Wikipedia, The Free Encyclopedia*, [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rascal\_(book)\&oldid=1316182702](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rascal_\(book\)\&oldid=1316182702).

² Christine Rousselle, "Japan grappling with invasive raccoon population," *Fox News*, May 18, 2024. [https://www.foxnews.com/lifestyle/japan-grappling-invasive-raccoon-population](https://www.foxnews.com/lifestyle/japan-grappling-invasive-raccoon-population).

frontmatter.title: Frozen Pumpkin Dessert Recipe
frontmatter.summary: A festive layered frozen dessert with ginger snap crust, vanilla ice cream, spiced pumpkin, and cool whip - perfect for fall celebrations!
frontmatter.author: Pam Hanson

articles.content:
# Frozen Pumpkin Dessert

*From Aunt Pam*\
*From the Kitchen of Pam Hanson*

## Ingredients

**Crust:**

* 2 cups ginger snap cookies, crumbled
* 6 tablespoons butter

**Layers:**

* Vanilla ice cream
* 2 cups pumpkin
* 1 cup sugar
* ½ cup brown sugar
* ½ teaspoon nutmeg
* ¼ teaspoon cloves
* 1 teaspoon cinnamon
* 8 ounces cool whip

## Instructions

1. Preheat oven to 350°F.
2. Prepare crust by putting crumbled ginger snaps in a 9x13 pan. Melt the butter, pour over the top, and combine cookies and butter well. Bake in preheated oven for 8 minutes. Set aside to cool.
3. Whip together in a medium sized bowl the pumpkin, sugar, brown sugar, nutmeg, cloves, and cinnamon.
4. Spread a 1 inch layer of vanilla ice cream on top of the cooled crust.
5. Spread finished pumpkin layer over the top of the ice cream.
6. Spread cool whip over the top of the pumpkin for the final layer.
7. Freeze the whole pan. When ready to serve, cut into squares and display your layers on a platter.

***

*This beautiful layered dessert is sure to impress at your next fall gathering!*

frontmatter.title: I Give You Lord My All
frontmatter.summary: An original poem about trusting God through loneliness, trials, and waiting - finding His presence and perfect peace in the storm.
frontmatter.author: Hope Hanson

articles.content:
# I Give You Lord My All

You meet me in the quiet lonely places\
Where the rain falls down like dust\
You whisper songs of comfort\
And quiet words of trust

You conquer every lie with truth\
And cast aside my fear\
And when I am at my loneliest\
Is when You, Lord, appear

My heart is in Your hands, my Lord\
My life is at Your call\
Make my desires only Yours\
I give You, Lord, my all

The howling wind and pouring rain\
Falls down hard and fast\
But Lord You promise deliverance\
And perfect joy at last

I wait for You, for in Your time\
You weave a kingdom song\
In every pause and every note\
Your melody grows strong

In the while, in this world\
There will be tears and pain\
There will be suffering and loss\
But He will come again

And so, my patient longing lasts\
But one day it will cease\
In fellowship with You at last\
And everlasting peace

***

*By Hope Hanson*

frontmatter.title: Inspiring Quotes from Christian Leaders
frontmatter.summary: Timeless wisdom from Sherwood Day, Jim Elliot, Corrie ten Boom, and A.W. Tozer on surrender, God's love, and trusting His plan.
frontmatter.author: Editorial Staff

articles.content:
# Inspiring Quotes from Christian Leaders

## On Surrender and God's Timing

> "A life abandoned to God cannot be cut short. 'Cut short' means not complete, interrupted, and we know that our Master does no half-way jobs."— **Sherwood Day**

***

> "God always gives His best to those who leave the choice with Him."— **Jim Elliot**

***

## On God's Purposes

> "Today I know that such memories are the key not to the past, but to the future. I know that the experiences of our lives, when we let God use them, become the mysterious and perfect preparation for the work he will give us to do."— **Corrie ten Boom**

***

## On God's Love

> "The love of God is one of the great realities of the universe, a pillar upon which the hope of the world rests. But it is a personal, intimate thing, too. God does not love populations, He loves people. He loves not masses, but men. He loves us all with a mighty love that has no beginning and can have no end."— **A.W. Tozer**

frontmatter.title: Media Reviews: Books and Music for October
frontmatter.summary: Reviews of Cody's Castle, Happy Little Family, and Hold Fast album - quality Christian content for children, young readers, and music lovers.
frontmatter.author: Joanna Rocke

articles.content:
# Media Reviews

## Children's Book: Cody's Castle

**by Gary Bower**

Cody learns about the importance of our words and how to love others by what we say on a summer trip to the beach. Come alongside Cody's mom and encourage your children too, with beautiful painted illustrations and follow-up questions included.

*— J. Rocke*

***

## Young Reader: Happy Little Family

**by Rebecca Caudill**

Long ago in the Kentucky Hills, four-year-old Bonnie wants to be a big girl and join in the action with her older siblings. Follow the Fairchild family in their scrapes and adventures and prepare to have fun! A great read for all ages or as a family read-aloud.

*— J. Rocke*

***

## Musical Album: Hold Fast

**by Steve Green**

Both majestic and beautiful, Steve Green masterfully weaves Psalms 113-116 into a Psalm Suite in the first four tracks. Each other track combines messages of truth and faith, concluding with "The Faith by Which We Stand," a solid finish to an impactful album.

*— J. Rocke*

***

## Book Challenge

Do you ever wonder how many books you've read in your lifetime? Or perhaps you can't remember the name of that really good book you finished last year and you can't find it again. Whatever the case is, there is an easy solution!

**My challenge to you is to keep a book journal.** Every time you finish a book, write down the Title and Author. For an extra bonus, write down your thoughts on the book! Other things to include could be the length of the book, genre, time it took you to finish it, or who recommended it to you. Be creative!

In the years to come, it will be fun to look back and see what you've read and how your reading habits have changed through the years. It's also fun to keep track of how many books you read in a year! My record was 66, maybe you can beat it!

Whatever you do, put your own special spin on it and have fun. Happy reading!

*— Hope Hanson*

# Win for WI: Milwaukee Brewers Win Central Division

The Milwaukee Brewers won the Central Division in the 2025 season, finishing 5 games ahead of their rival, the Chicago Cubs. The team broke several records, including a franchise win streak with 14 wins in August.

## Record-Breaking Performance

Their exceptional base running contributed extensively to the historic season. The Brewers demonstrated outstanding teamwork and athletic prowess throughout the year, culminating in one of the best seasons in franchise history.

## A Tribute to Bob Ueker

For many fans and players alike, the phenomenal season serves as a tribute to the legacy of the late Bob Ueker, who passed away in January 2025. Ueker's decades-long association with the Brewers as the beloved voice of the team left an indelible mark on Wisconsin baseball culture.

The 2025 championship run reminded fans across Wisconsin why they love America's pastime and why the Brewers hold a special place in the hearts of Badger State residents.

***

*Go Brewers!*

frontmatter.title: On Prayer: Search Me, O God
frontmatter.summary: Prayer is one of the most crucial aspects of Christian life. Start with humility and surrender using Psalm 139:23-24 as a guide.
frontmatter.author: Joanna Rocke

articles.content:
# On Prayer

Prayer is by far one of the most crucial aspects of the Christian life. How are we to know God, be transformed to be like Christ, or battle for Him, if we never talk to Him? Indeed, half the battle is won when we put our lives into His hands instead of holding on to it ourselves. We should know by now that it is foolish to hold onto control!

I have found praying Psalm 139:23-24 to be a great place to start as I humble myself and turn to God. As you pray in the next weeks, try praying this scripture and allow God to convict you of sin and restore you to truth.

> "Search me, O God, and know my heart; try me, and know my anxieties; and see if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting."*Psalm 139:23-24*

frontmatter.title: Position Changes Everything
frontmatter.summary: Understanding our position in Christ - seated in heavenly places with all authority - is the key to living victoriously and becoming a spiritual monument for this generation.
frontmatter.author: Joanna Rocke

articles.content:
# Position Changes Everything

Monuments. We see them everywhere. The Acropolis. Stonehenge. Mount Rushmore. Machu Picchu. Big Ben. The Statue of Liberty. Statues in the Capitol Rotunda. Small town memorials for veterans. We call them monuments for a reason. They are the products of ages and nations. They pay tribute to something that made a mark upon the world, whether great or evil. We look on these monuments today and learn about the people who built them.

## Called to Be Monuments

Like these monuments, God wants us, the church, to be a monument too. Through us, He can show the world something of Himself that they will never see elsewhere. He can do something in the weak, tenuous, feeble, followers of His that makes them strong. He can cause His glory to shine through them in such a way that the world can't help but stop and say, "Did you see that?!"

## The Power of Remembering

Throughout this issue, you will find the theme of reflecting. Reflecting or remembering is important. It makes us pause and evaluate where we are going. Again and again in the Bible, we are told to remember. In fact, the word 'remember' appears over 1200 times in the Bible. However, God doesn't want us to just relive memories and talk about past events for fun. Those spiritual monuments of the past serve as a forward call. They urge us to turn toward God with a renewed zeal. It is almost ironic. The monuments of the past open the door of opportunity for us to become monuments ourselves.

That is why this newspaper is called Monumental Times. We want to remember the spiritual monuments of the past with the intent to build the current era of the church into a monumental time in history. It starts with us looking back, but it doesn't end there. Remembering takes time and some effort, but what does it mean to be a monumental era of history?

## Understanding Our Position

I believe it all starts with understanding (or remembering) who we are, who God is, and what our position is. We are sinners who rebelled against God. God is a perfect and holy God who is not anything like us. He came and died for our sin so that we wouldn't have to – but He took it further. He gave us His perfect righteousness and spotless reputation and took our sin-scarred one. Then, He came back to life so that we can have His power in us to win the victory over sin.

When we accept His death on our behalf, we enter into Him, and we go where He goes. Our sin nature died with Him, and we rise to new life in Him. The journey doesn't end there. He ascended to heaven and sits at the right hand of the Father. If we are in Him, we sit there with Him too. Ephesians tells us exactly where Christ went:

> "The working of His mighty power which He worked in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly places, far above all principality and power and might and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in that which is to come. And He put all things under His feet, and gave Him to be head over all things to the church, which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all in all."*Ephesians 1:19-23*

## We Are There Too

Ephesians then tells us we are there too because we are in Christ:

> "But God, who is rich in mercy, because of His great love with which He loved us, even when we were dead in trespasses, made us alive together with Christ (by grace you have been saved), and raised us up together, and made us sit together in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus, that in the ages to come He might show the exceeding riches of His grace in His kindness toward us in Christ Jesus."*Ephesians 2:4-7*

This is where you are if you are in Christ! You are seated over all authorities and powers because you are IN CHRIST! Be reminded, it is not any of your doing and you do not deserve to be there, but the facts remain. You are there in Christ. The power of sin in your life is gone. Why do you fear? You, in Christ, are over all things. He has all authority. We act like we are drowning when we are already in the boat! Why? Do not let sin rule! You are IN CHRIST.

## Living in Two Realms

Christ's physical man is in heaven, but His spirit is in you. Your physical man is here, but your spiritual man is in Christ, in heaven. You are in heaven, seated over all things, now. Think about it. You are there this moment. It is not a someday or sometime. It is now. Let this truth sink into your hearts. Let it change your life.

## A Monumental Generation

When a generation of the church grasps this – the power of their position in Christ – the world will be changed. That generation will become a spiritual monument for that age and ages to come. God is looking for Christians who understand the gospel and live it out. He can accomplish His purposes for His glory through them, because they will be bravehearted and bending to His will.

> "Now to Him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us, to Him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus to all generations, forever and ever. Amen."*Ephesians 3:20-21*

***

## Author's Note

The theme of knowing your position is something that God has put into my life the past few years. It is something I need to remember every minute but so often forget. There are two things I would highly recommend for you:

1. **Memorize parts of Ephesians 1 and 2** or even the first few chapters. I began memorizing the whole book several years ago and while I didn't finish all six chapters then, I did memorize the first three. Having that word in your heart is powerful and it helps you anchor your heart to truth.
2. Watch the **'Reckoning the Truth' video series** (2 videos) available on YouTube from Ellerslie Discipleship Training. They expound on the theme of position in a short amount of time.

frontmatter.title: Book Review: Shadow of the Almighty
frontmatter.summary: A powerful review of Elisabeth Elliot's compilation of Jim Elliot's journals and letters - a must-read for anyone seeking to deepen their faith and live wholeheartedly for God.
frontmatter.author: Hope Hanson

articles.content:
# Shadow of the Almighty
## The Life & Testament of Jim Elliot
**By Elisabeth Elliot**

Jim Elliot was young, passionate, and on fire for the Lord, taking advantage of every opportunity for the glory of God. Through life's ups and downs, he steadfastly dedicated his 28 years to the work of the Lord before paying the ultimate price for his sacrifice.

## A Legacy in Words

Elisabeth Elliot, Jim Elliot's wife, masterfully compiled the letters and journal entries from Jim Elliot after his death in 1956, compiling the thoughts, struggles, breakthroughs, and passions of a young man with a driving purpose. When I first picked up this book, I wasn't sure whether to expect the same old run-of-the-mill story I'd heard so many times before. But reading through Jim Elliot's writings impacted me more than I imagined.

## Lessons from a Life Well-Lived

Jim Elliot wrote especially throughout his years going to school and while preparing for the missionary journey to Ecuador that would eventually take his life. Each lesson he learned in trusting the Lord and leaning on his Savior in every situation was a lesson for me as well, and I was refreshed and renewed in my desire to know the Lord more and keep pressing into my faith.

## My Recommendation

I highly recommend reading this book, or listening to it read by Elisabeth Elliot herself. If you allow your heart and mind to be open to the Lord's work, there is no telling how *Shadow of the Almighty* could minister to you as well.

**Recommended for ages 16 and up.**

---

*"He is no fool who gives what he cannot keep to gain that which he cannot lose." — Jim Elliot*

frontmatter.title: S'mores Bars Recipe
frontmatter.summary: Easy and delicious S'mores Bars featuring graham crackers, caramel, chocolate chips, and marshmallows - perfect for fall gatherings!
frontmatter.author: Pam Hanson

articles.content:
# S'mores Bars

*From Cook's Country Magazine*\
*From the Kitchen of Pam Hanson*

## Ingredients

* Graham Crackers
* 5 tablespoons butter (unsalted)
* ¼ cup brown sugar
* ½ teaspoon salt
* ½ cup milk chocolate chips
* Mini marshmallows

## Instructions

1. Preheat oven to 375°F.
2. Line an 8x8 square pan with graham crackers. Make them fit carefully and break off any graham crackers that don't fit if needed.
3. For the caramel mixture, heat the butter, brown sugar, and salt together in a pan until boiling. Pour the mixture over the graham crackers when finished.
4. Spread chocolate chips over the top of the caramel mixture.
5. Bake in preheated oven for 10 minutes until it bubbles.
6. Take out of oven and sprinkle top with mini marshmallows.
7. Cool in freezer. Once cooled, break into pieces and serve.

***

*Enjoy this campfire classic in bar form!*

frontmatter.title: Welcome to Monumental Times!
frontmatter.summary: Discover the vision behind this new publication - a call to remember God's work in our lives through stories, testimonies, and spiritual truths.
frontmatter.author: Hope Hanson

articles.content:
# Welcome to Monumental Times!

You have happened upon the inaugural issue of a new, up-and-coming newspaper filled with all your favorite things – stories, testimonies, quotes, laughs, and more! Where did it all come from? I'm glad you asked.

## The Biblical Foundation of Remembering

Throughout the Bible, God has always emphasized the importance of remembering. He commanded the Israelites to set up monuments of stone to mark significant moments in their history (Joshua 4:1-24). He reminded them time and time again to write scripture on our hearts (Jeremiah 31:33). Much of the Bible itself is full of historical accounts reminding us of God's work throughout the ages.

## Inspired by Amy Carmichael

Amy Carmichael, missionary to India in the early 1900s, recognized how important this was. When she still lived in Ireland and England, she published a small magazine called "Scraps" to remind family and friends of spiritual truths. Looking back at "Scraps" is one of the ways we can look into the life of the missionary and see how God brought her from there to eventually impacting so many lives in India.

## Our Vision: Remember!

This newspaper began with that same vision in mind: remembering what God has done. Far too often in our busy lives we forget to remember the things God is working all around us. In this publication you will find that everything written or created has that driving purpose behind it: **Remember!**

It is a call to be intentional, to write down and record in our own "piles of stones" what our Father in heaven is doing among His children... those Monumental moments in our lives.

## Join Us on This Journey

So, sit back, relax, and remember with us as we press on to chronicle our faith and wield our pen as valiant warriors in a world so prone to forget.

***

*Hope Hanson is the founder and editor of Monumental Times.*

frontmatter.title: The ''Unprofitable Servant'': William Wilberforce
frontmatter.summary: The remarkable story of William Wilberforce - from frivolous college student to champion of abolition, whose faith and persistence changed England forever.
frontmatter.author: Hannah Rocke

articles.content:
# The "Unprofitable Servant": William Wilberforce

Tenacity. Courage. Virtue. Winsomeness. Devotion. Integrity. Humility. The enduring trademarks of a man whose accomplishments and fame were more than matched by his character. His nation had forgotten her Christian heritage and was sliding into deeper spiritual and social decay when he realized that God had called him to take a stand. Using all the influence he could command, he strove to bring reform: not merely in cultural norms and laws, but in the very hearts and minds of his countrymen. Resistance was intense and progress slow, but he was faithful to his principles and purposes. And when success eventually crowned his endeavors, he remained untainted by pride, seeing himself as merely an "unprofitable servant" of the Lord.

## Early Life and Conversion

Born in the port city of Hull on August 4, 1759, William was a frail child with weak eyes. Although he battled physical ailments all his life, his lively mind, personal charm, and kind nature were never hampered. After his aunt and uncle exposed him to true Christianity, William's mother whisked him away to a life of frivolity and pleasure, hoping to protect her son from "enthusiasm."

His years at Cambridge and St. John's College were largely frittered away on card parties and idle amusements. Innately witty, charming, and musical, he became the most popular man on campus. Even after his election to Parliament, his pleasure-seeking ways continued, fed by the estate inherited from his father and uncle. He and his friend William Pitt joined clubs, socialized with the elite, and partied as if they were still in college.

Largely due to the force of his magnetic personality and persuasive speech, he influenced Pitt's election to prime minister and won the prestigious Yorkshire seat for himself. At 24, William had a life anyone in England might covet. Yet God used a "coincidence" to radically change his life.

## The Turning Point

After running into friend Isaac Milner, William invited him on a journey to the Franco-Italian Rivera. During this time, William and Isaac discussed spiritual matters. As they talked, William's flippancy turned to interest, then intellectual assent, and finally true belief. He wrestled intensely with his own sinfulness and marveled in the sufficient, atoning work of Christ.

William decided his conversion required withdrawal from government. He wrote to his friend and prime minister, Pitt. Pitt wasn't a Christian, but he challenged William's view, pointing out that Christian principles should lead to action, not only meditation. But, despite Pitt's best efforts to dissuade him, William staunchly held to his new-found conviction.

## Meeting John Newton

However, before making a decision, he sought godly counsel. On December 7, 1785, he met with a former slave-ship captain, John Newton. After his life was transformed by the gospel, John had eventually become a minister, also penning the now-famous hymn "Amazing Grace." John encouraged William to remain in his elected position, suggesting that God had placed him there for the good of the church and nation.

## A Two-Fold Calling

With new consecration to God and a vision for how his parliamentary position could be used, William's eyes were quickly opened to opportunities. On every level, England had spiraled into moral debauchery: immorality, drunkenness, gambling, dueling, prostitution, and corruption were rampant. William began to fight these issues wherever he could. After a small group of abolitionists begged him to become their parliamentary leader, William hesitated feeling a better-qualified person could be found. Yet after spending time praying and studying in his library on a rainy day, he felt an unmistakable call from God. William knew he had a two-fold purpose: the abolition of the slave trade and the reformation of English culture.

## Fighting for Change

Only those who have struggled for change in a cultural mindset can possibly know the heartbreaking, exhausting work God had placed before William. Through his book, *A Practical View of Christianity*, William outlined what he believed England needed most: not a return to a moral standard, a spirit of love and kindness for other people, or a new kind of government. He preached the gospel boldly in his book, showing what a truly Christian life should look like.

He also endeavored to change the social climate in other tangible ways. Not limiting himself to speeches and laws, he founded an organization and enlisted influential men to partner with him. When the king issued a proclamation calling for social reform, William used the opportunity to personally urge civil and church leaders to join the cause.

Any efforts to curtail the slave trade were constantly stymied and voted down. Political power, monetary gain, fear of revolt, and a wariness of anything smelling of fanaticism motivated opposition. But William had a strength of resolve and patient persistence rivaled by few. He quietly whittled away at public opinion with speeches and pamphlets, always taking small victories where he could win them.

## Family and Personal Life

William's strength of character wasn't limited to his public life. After a whirlwind courtship, William married Barbara Spooner on May 30, 1797 and they had two girls and three boys. Extremely devoted, he delighted in his family and encouraged them to pursue the Lord. When he felt his position kept him away from them too much, he resigned his seat in Yorkshire for one with less importance and responsibility.

His relationship with God remained the mainspring of his activity and he spent hours in study and prayer, creating lists of friends he was praying for. He also jotted notes about ways to have spiritual conversations with them. He cut out amusements that distracted him or wasted time and journaled about his spiritual life. Gregarious and charming to the end, his fun-loving, agreeable nature was tempered with a consecration that left an impression on all who knew him.

## Victory and Legacy

Through long years of poor health, disappointments, uncertainty, and setbacks, he continued to faithfully pursue what God had set before him. His influence brought great change in England as he championed for reform in prisons, legal punishment, factories, elections, and more. And after a decades-long fight, he saw the slave trade abolished by law on March 25, 1807. Tremendously thankful, he then turned his attention to the institution of slavery.

William retired from Parliament in 1825 due to failing health. He spent his last years living with one of his children after paying his son's debt incurred from a failed business venture. But leaving public life never removed him from the fight. He kept up correspondence and gave occasional speeches, giving his last address a mere three months before his death.

As he lay on his deathbed in 1833, word was brought to him of the abolition of slavery and the emancipation of the slaves, a fitting sendoff to the champion of the slaves.

As news of the bill spread through the English empire, William Wilberforce left this world on July 29th. Generations later, he is still heralded as a great social reformer and man of faith, undoubtedly hearing his Creator declare "Well done, good and faithful servant."

***

## Further Reading

* **Statesman and Saint: The Principled Politics of William Wilberforce** by David J. Vaughan
* **A Practical View of Christianity** by William Wilberforce
